examples.en: It's better to care about substance than appearance.
Even if it looks great outside, the inside matters.
This fruit doesn't look good, but it tastes delicious.
Don't judge just by outward appearance.
They only changed the outside, so it looks like a new car.
The two products look alike on the outside, so I got confused.

explain: '겉모습'과 거의 같고, 물건이나 음식의 바깥 모양을 말할 때 잘 어울려요. 사람에게는 '겉모습'이나 '외모'도 써요. 반대로 안쪽은 '속'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is almost the same as '겉모습' and fits the outer look of objects and food. For people, '겉모습' or '외모' is also used. The inside is called '속'.

examples.ko: 이 뮤지컬은 매일 저녁 서울에서 공연돼요.
examples.en: This musical is performed in Seoul every evening.
That play was staged in Seoul last month.

examples.ko: 새 콘서트가 다음 달부터 공연될 거예요.
examples.en: The new concert will be performed starting next month.

examples.ko: 공연되는 동안에는 사진을 찍으면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not take photos while it is being performed.

examples.ko: 학교 강당에서 학생 연극이 공연되면 보러 갈래요?
examples.en: If a student play is staged in the school hall, do you want to go see it?

examples.ko: 이 작품은 세계 여러 나라에서 공연되고 있어요.
examples.en: This work is being performed in many countries around the world.

explain: '공연하다'는 무대에서 연주하거나 연기하는 쪽이고, '공연되다'는 작품이 무대에 올라가는 것이에요. 영화는 '상영되다', TV와 라디오는 '방송되다'라고 구분해요. 뮤지컬·연극·콘서트·발레에 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: '공연하다' is the side performing on stage; '공연되다' is a work being put on stage. Movies are '상영되다', and TV and radio are '방송되다'. It fits musicals, plays, concerts and ballet.

dis.h: a show or concert is staged

p.n: 상연되다 is more written and formal; it also covers films.

examples.en: My younger sibling attends a national university.
National universities tend to have lower tuition than private ones.
A professor from a national university came to give a special lecture.

examples.ko: 우리 지역 국립대가 새 캠퍼스를 열었어요.
examples.en: Our region's national university opened a new campus.

examples.ko: 국립대와 사립대 중 어디가 더 좋아요?
examples.en: Which is better, a national or a private university?
I graduated from a national university and work in my hometown.

explain: '국립대학교'를 줄인 말이에요. 반대되는 말은 '사립대'예요.
explain_en: It is a shortened form of '국립대학교'. Its opposite is '사립대' (private university).

examples.ko: 이 책은 청소년 독자층을 겨냥해서 만들었어요.
examples.en: This book was made with teenage readers in mind.
The readership is broad, so anyone can read it easily.
The new novel is popular among readers in their twenties.

examples.ko: 독자층에 따라 글의 말투를 바꿔야 해요.
examples.en: You have to change the tone of the writing depending on the readership.
The readership is gradually getting older.

examples.ko: 독자층도 달라서 두 책의 분위기가 달라요.
examples.en: The readerships differ too, so the two books feel different.

explain: '독자'는 읽는 사람 하나하나이고, '독자층'은 나이나 취향이 비슷한 읽는 사람들의 무리예요. 책, 잡지, 웹툰을 이야기할 때 '독자층이 넓다/좁다'로 자주 써요.
explain_en: '독자' means individual readers, while '독자층' is a group of readers with similar age or taste. It is often used with books, magazines and webtoons, as in '독자층이 넓다/좁다'.

examples.en: The new phone has a very bright display.
The staff changed the product display in the store.
The battery status appears on the display.
There is a model inside the glass display.

examples.ko: 디스플레이는 크기가 너무 작은 것 같아요.
examples.en: The display seems too small.
The display looked nice, so I went into the shop.

explain: 화면 장치도, 가게에서 물건을 보기 좋게 늘어놓는 일도 디스플레이라고 해요. 장치는 '화면', 늘어놓는 일은 '진열'로 바꿔 말할 수 있어요.
explain_en: Both a screen device and the arrangement of goods in a shop are called 'diseupeullei'. The device can be said as '화면' and the arranging as '진열'.

examples.ko: 이 노래는 인기 랭킹 일 위예요.
examples.en: This song is number one in the popularity ranking.
The school's ranking rose a lot from last year.
To check the ranking, open the app.
I found my name on the game ranking.

examples.ko: 맛집 랭킹 사이트를 보고 식당을 골랐어요.
examples.en: I picked a restaurant after looking at a restaurant ranking site.
I study while competing on the ranking with a friend.

explain: '순위'는 몇 번째인지 숫자 자리를 말하고, '랭킹'은 그 순위를 매긴 목록 전체를 말할 때가 많아요. 그래서 '순위가 올랐어요', '랭킹에 들었어요'처럼 말해요. 앱과 인터넷 글에서는 '랭킹'이 아주 흔해요.
explain_en: '순위' is the numbered place, whereas '랭킹' often refers to the whole ranked list, hence '순위가 올랐어요' (my place went up) and '랭킹에 들었어요' (I made the list). In apps and online posts '랭킹' is very common.

examples.ko: 이 코트는 물세탁이 안 돼서 세탁소에 맡겼어요.
examples.en: This coat can't be washed in water, so I left it at the cleaners.

examples.ko: 라벨을 보니까 물세탁을 해도 된다고 써 있어요.
examples.en: The label says it's okay to wash it in water.

examples.ko: 울 스웨터는 물세탁하면 줄어들 수 있어요.
examples.en: A wool sweater can shrink if you wash it in water.

examples.ko: 물세탁은 차가운 물로 살살 해야 해요.
examples.en: Washing in water should be done gently with cold water.

examples.ko: 운동화는 물세탁하기 전에 먼저 먼지를 털어 주세요.
examples.en: Before washing sneakers in water, shake off the dust first.

examples.ko: 이불은 집에서 물세탁으로 빨기에는 너무 커요.
examples.en: A blanket is too big to wash in water at home.

explain: 반대는 '드라이클리닝'이에요. 옷 라벨에서 자주 보는 말이고, '물세탁하다'처럼 동사로도 써요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '드라이클리닝' (dry cleaning). You often see it on clothing labels, and it works as a verb too: '물세탁하다'.

examples.ko: 커피에 백설탕을 한 숟가락 넣어 주세요.
examples.en: Please put one spoonful of white sugar in my coffee.

examples.ko: 요리할 때 백설탕 대신 꿀을 써도 돼요.
examples.en: When cooking, you can use honey instead of white sugar.

examples.ko: 백설탕이 다 떨어져서 마트에 가야 해요.
examples.en: We've run out of white sugar, so I have to go to the supermarket.

examples.ko: 쿠키를 만들려면 백설탕 이백 그램이 필요해요.
examples.en: To make cookies, you need two hundred grams of white sugar.

examples.ko: 백설탕을 너무 많이 먹으면 몸에 안 좋아요.
examples.en: Eating too much white sugar is bad for your body.
A lot of white sugar went into this cake.

explain: 색이 하얀 설탕이라서 갈색인 '황설탕'이나 검은 '흑설탕'과 비교할 때 써요. 평소에는 그냥 '설탕'이라고 하는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It is the white sugar, used when you compare it with brown '황설탕' or dark '흑설탕'. In everyday talk people often just say '설탕'.

examples.ko: 이사하고 나서 제 생활이 백팔십도 달라졌어요.
examples.en: After moving, my life changed completely.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 노래 스타일을 백팔십도 바꿨어요.
examples.en: That singer completely changed his singing style.
While driving, I made a U-turn and went back.

examples.ko: 어제 한 말과 오늘 하는 말이 백팔십도 달라요.
examples.en: What you said yesterday and what you say today are totally different.

examples.ko: 거울 앞에서 몸을 백팔십도 돌려 보세요.
examples.en: Try turning your body 180 degrees in front of the mirror.

examples.ko: 시험에 합격한 뒤로 부모님 태도가 백팔십도 변했어요.
examples.en: After I passed the exam, my parents' attitude did a complete turnaround.

explain: 각도 그대로 몸이나 방향을 돌릴 때도 쓰지만, '정반대로'라는 뜻으로 더 많이 써요. 보통 '달라지다, 바뀌다, 변하다'와 함께 와요. 숫자로 '180도'라고 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: It can mean a literal 180-degree turn, but it is more often used to mean 'the complete opposite'. It usually appears with '달라지다', '바뀌다' or '변하다'. It can also be written with numerals as '180도'.

examples.en: In springtime my nose itches because of pollen.
When springtime comes, there are more people in the mountains.
Spring weather is chilly in the morning and evening.
Every spring we go to see the flowers with my family.
Yellow dust in springtime is not good for your health.
Both spring and fall are good for traveling.

explain: '철'은 한 계절이나 어떤 시기를 뜻해서 '여름철', '장마철', '휴가철'처럼 써요. '봄'은 계절 이름이고, 봄철은 '봄철 건강', '봄철 황사'처럼 봄에 생기는 일과 함께 써요.
explain_en: '철' means a season or a period of the year, as in '여름철', '장마철' and '휴가철'. '봄' is the name of the season, and 봄철 goes with things that happen in spring, like '봄철 건강' and '봄철 황사'.

examples.en: I compared the tuition of private and national universities.
My younger sibling got into a private university in Seoul.
I'm looking into scholarships at private universities now.

examples.ko: 이 지역에는 사립대가 세 곳 있어요.
examples.en: There are three private universities in this area.

examples.ko: 사립대 출신이라고 해서 불리한 건 아니에요.
examples.en: Coming from a private university isn't a disadvantage.
My older sister graduated from a private university and joined a company.

explain: '사립대학교'를 줄인 말이고, 짝말은 '국립대'예요. 대학 이야기를 할 때 '사립대'와 '국립대'를 나눠서 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It is a short form of '사립대학교', and its counterpart is '국립대' (national university). When people talk about universities, they often divide them into '사립대' and '국립대'.

examples.en: This factory produces cars.
The farmers produced rice.
This year they'll produce a lot of apples.
There are several ways to produce electricity.
I bought a product made in Korea.
We're producing a thousand a day.

explain: 공장이나 농장에서 물건을 만들어 낼 때 써요. 파는 쪽의 '판매하다', 사는 쪽의 '소비하다'와 한 묶음으로 자주 나와요. 개인이 만든 작은 물건에는 '만들다'가 자연스러워요.
explain_en: Used when a factory or farm turns out goods. It often appears in a set with the verb for selling and the one for consuming. For small things an individual makes, the plain verb for 'make' sounds more natural.

dis.h: make goods or crops in quantity

p.n: 제조하다 focuses on manufacturing in a factory; 생산하다 is broader.

examples.ko: 시골길에서 소 한 마리가 천천히 걸어가요.
examples.en: A cow is slowly walking along the country road.

examples.ko: 번잡한 도심을 벗어나 한적한 시골길을 달렸어요.
examples.en: I left the busy city and drove along a quiet country road.
Country roads get really dark at night.

examples.ko: 할머니 댁에 가는 시골길이 아주 좁아요.
examples.en: The country road to my grandmother's house is very narrow.
Cosmos flowers are blooming along the country road.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날 시골길은 진흙투성이가 돼요.
examples.en: On rainy days, country roads get covered in mud.

explain: '시골길을 걷다', '시골길을 달리다'처럼 써요. 도시의 길은 보통 '큰길', '골목길'처럼 다르게 불러요.
explain_en: It is used as '시골길을 걷다' (walk along a country road) or '시골길을 달리다' (drive along one). Roads in a city are usually called other things, such as '큰길' (main road) or '골목길' (alley).

examples.ko: 커피에 시럽 한 번만 넣어 주세요.
examples.en: Please add just one pump of syrup to my coffee.

examples.ko: 팬케이크 위에 메이플 시럽을 듬뿍 뿌렸어요.
examples.en: I poured plenty of maple syrup on the pancakes.
Syrup is too sweet, so I add only a little.

examples.ko: 기침 시럽에는 단맛이 있어서 아이들이 잘 먹어요.
examples.en: Cough syrup is sweet, so children take it well.

examples.ko: 시럽이 다 떨어져서 새로 사야 해요.
examples.en: The syrup ran out, so I need to buy more.
I made shaved ice with strawberry syrup.

explain: 카페에서는 '시럽 추가'처럼 단맛을 더하는 액체를 말해요. 약국에서 파는 달콤한 물약 중에도 '시럽'이라고 부르는 것이 있어요.
explain_en: At cafes it is the sweet liquid you add, as in 시럽 추가. Some sweet liquid medicines sold at pharmacies are also called 시럽.

examples.en: My father bought a new car this month.
The color of this new car is really cool.
When a new car comes out, pictures are posted online.
Many reporters gathered at the new car launch event.
Many people buy used cars rather than new ones.

examples.ko: 회사 앞에 신차로 보이는 하얀 차가 서 있어요.
examples.en: A white car that looks brand new is parked in front of the office.

explain: 반대는 '중고차'예요. 친구와 이야기할 때는 '새 차'라고 하는 경우가 많고, 신차는 '신차 출시', '신차 발표'처럼 뉴스나 광고에 어울려요. '신제품'의 '신'도 같은 글자예요.
explain_en: The opposite is '중고차'. Talking with a friend, people often say '새 차', while 신차 fits news and ads, as in '신차 출시' and '신차 발표'. The '신' is the same character as in '신제품'.

examples.en: I collect aluminium cans separately and throw them out.
This pot is made of aluminium.
Aluminium was used for the bicycle frame.
Aluminium is light and does not rust easily.
Cans are made of aluminium and iron.
Aluminium can be recycled too.

explain: 음식을 싸는 얇은 종이 같은 것은 '은박지' 또는 '호일'이라고 해요. 알루미늄은 재료 이름이라 '알루미늄 캔'처럼 뒤에 물건 이름을 붙여 써요.
explain_en: The thin sheet for wrapping food is called 'eunbakji' or 'hoil'. Aluminium is a material name, so it comes before an object name, as in 'aluminium can'.

examples.en: Seoul is a city with a very large population.
I surveyed the city's population and put it in a table.

examples.ko: 이 마을의 인구수는 해마다 줄고 있어요.
examples.en: This village's population is getting smaller every year.

examples.ko: 인구수에 맞게 학교를 더 지어야 해요.
examples.en: We need to build more schools to match the population.
Please compare the population and the area together.
In terms of population, Busan comes after Seoul.

explain: '인구가 많아요'처럼 '인구'만 써도 같은 뜻이에요. 인구수는 사람 수를 숫자로 말할 때 어울려요. 사람은 '명'으로 세서 '인구 백만 명'이라고 해요.
explain_en: You can say just '인구' as in '인구가 많아요' with the same meaning. 인구수 fits when you talk about the number itself. People are counted with '명', as in '인구 백만 명'.

examples.en: The child has a candy in their mouth.
Would you like a piece of candy, sir?
I handed out candy to children on Halloween.
This candy is strawberry flavored.

examples.ko: 캔디를 너무 많이 먹어서 이가 아파요.
examples.en: I ate too much candy, so my tooth hurts.

examples.ko: 비행기에서 귀가 아플 때 캔디를 먹어요.
examples.en: When my ears hurt on a plane, I eat candy.

explain: 일상에서 가장 자연스러운 말은 '사탕'이에요. '캔디'는 포장지나 가게 이름, 영어식 느낌을 주고 싶을 때 자주 보여요. '사탕을 입에 물다', '사탕을 빨아 먹다'처럼 말하고, 막대에 달린 건 '막대사탕', 솜 같은 건 '솜사탕'이라고 해요.
explain_en: The most natural everyday word is 사탕. 캔디 appears more on packages, shop names, or when you want an English feel. People say '사탕을 입에 물다' and '사탕을 빨아 먹다'. A lollipop is 막대사탕 and cotton candy is 솜사탕.

examples.en: Saturn has large rings around it.
I looked at Saturn through a telescope.

examples.ko: 토성에는 아직 사람이 가 본 적이 없어요.
examples.en: No human has been to Saturn yet.
Saturn looked bright in the night sky.

examples.ko: 토성의 고리는 얼음과 돌로 되어 있어요.
examples.en: Saturn's rings are made of ice and rock.
Saturn is a very big planet like Jupiter.

explain: 토성의 '토'는 토요일의 '토'(흙)와 같은 글자예요. 목성은 목요일의 '목'(나무)처럼 행성 이름과 요일 이름이 이어져요.
explain_en: The 토 in 토성 is the same character as the 토 (earth) in 토요일. Likewise 목성 shares 목 (wood) with 목요일, so planet names and weekday names are linked.

examples.en: Our class has thirty students in total.
The class was split into two this year.
The school set up a new class.
I joined the third-year class.
The atmosphere in the class is really good.

examples.ko: 우리는 옆 학급과 축구 시합을 했어요.
examples.en: We played a soccer match against the next class.

explain: 일상에서는 '반'이 훨씬 자주 나와요. '1학년 3반'처럼 말하고, '학급'은 '학급 회의', '학급 문고'처럼 학교 안의 공식적인 말에 잘 나와요.
explain_en: In daily life '반' is far more common, as in '1학년 3반'. '학급' appears in more official school phrases such as '학급 회의' and '학급 문고'.
